changed: Survey sharing opens the output choices directly: Copy link, QR code or Print invitations explicitly confirms issuance after access and revocation disclosure.
fixed: Copy and print failures reuse the received in-memory link; uncertain issuance never retries automatically, and stale identity/page responses cannot reveal credentials.
security: Existing preview/execute/revoke APIs, role checks and one-time link disclosure remain unchanged; no credential persistence or background issuance.

added: Signed-in users can send optional app feedback from the current shell with a separate form and a confirmed feedback reference.
changed: Persona evidence includes three historical local-browser form cases and current automated HTTP/MCP expiry and form regressions; human satisfaction, confusion and frustration are NOT MEASURED.
fixed: Entered feedback survives refused or uncertain submissions; the form requests authenticated attribution at the actual write boundary instead of relying on cached sign-in.
security: Optional require_authenticated on the existing HTTP/MCP feedback write refuses anonymous callers before persistence when true; omission or false preserves public feedback. No database migration or automatic context capture.

added: Compact action-specific MCP cards for metadata, entity reads, feedback acknowledgement, refusal and explicit dangerous-action confirmation.
Requested survey template results display the returned questionnaire, options, version and perspective read-only, instead of a generic success card.
changed: Docs orientation is text-only. Panel startup waits for the host call and does not automatically fetch identity, workspaces or projects; full exploration requires an explicit action.

Six bounded official-host scenarios are covered across attributed pre/post-fix sources; the final integrated theme/card host check passed1/1 independently. Human satisfaction, confusion and frustration are NOT MEASURED.
fixed: Compact confirmations show server-owned impact, affected targets, compensating control and expiry; busy and one-shot execution guards remain enforced.
security: The existing four-tool contract and server authorization remain unchanged. Private feedback and authorization details are not echoed in cards; no automatic execute or retry.

changed: Theme scorecard: 6/6 automated local scenarios and 4/4 bounded official reference-host visual scenarios passed; human satisfaction, confusion and frustration are NOT MEASURED.
fixed: The MCP panel follows the host light/dark theme with operating-system fallback and live updates; a local System/Light/Dark override takes precedence.
security: Theme changes do not invoke tools or change authentication, permissions, confirmations or persisted product data.

changed: Persona outcome scorecard records five executed route cases and one independent local-browser participant-resume journey; human sentiment remains NOT MEASURED.
fixed: Current-shell participant resume opens the preserved legacy survey instead of returning an existing participant session to the public access-code entry.
security: Route forwarding does not read, modify or expose participant credentials. Existing public survey, shared-link, invitation and synthetic-demo routes retain their behavior.

fixed: Release validation runs all 34 synthetic report contexts as sequential bounded cases, preserves the 425-response aggregate and coexistence checks, and drains or quarantines unfinished fixture work before reuse.

added: A source-pinned synthetic assessment example with three surveys, twelve responses, an inspectable report and sample answers, using the real assessment/report/participant UI.
An isolated sample survey with the real question, review, edit and receipt flow; practice answers stay in memory and are never submitted to a live API.
changed: Public tour and sample links, including the direct legacy example URL, use the shared application screens. The legacy homepage's overall visual design is preserved.
Generic legacy navigation is retired where current screens exist; invitation acceptance and access-code participation remain compatible.
The eight-check browser plan is closed with separately attributed historical and independent exact-head local evidence; real-human satisfaction, confusion and frustration remain NOT MEASURED.
fixed: The legacy sample assessment no longer promises a populated assessment while displaying only narrative stage descriptions.
security: Demo transport rejects unknown reads and all assessment mutations without network fallback. It does not read or change real staff credentials or participant drafts.

added: Synthetic report preview and explicit confirmed build in the current assessment Understand view, followed by refreshed report list and reopen.
changed: Canonical release notes include the bounded reporting persona outcome scorecard, distinguishing automated local outcomes from unmeasured human and agent journeys.
security: Existing synthetic admission and exact assessment grants remain authoritative; held inputs, expired previews, identity/navigation changes and uncertain writes do not enable automatic execution or retry.

changed: Release notes include a bounded persona outcome scorecard; human satisfaction remains not measured.
fixed: Initial host-initiated MCP read refusals appear in the panel without leaking private error details; navigation clears the refusal.

added: Canonical DEV domain dev.3dreview.app and production domain 3dreview.app on the existing Workers, with previous addresses retained as compatible aliases.
changed: Invitation emails use the canonical origin for their environment; browser-created participant links remain on the current origin.

Persona evidence backfill: operator browser sign-in reached the workspace page on 2/2 canonical environments (DEV and production); full persona workflows and real-user satisfaction, confusion and frustration NOT MEASURED. See the Persona outcome scorecard in releases/0.7.0.md.
security: Existing authentication audiences, host-only sessions, OAuth callback validation and participant fragment handling remain unchanged. New sign-in paths require matching Cloudflare Access destinations.

changed: Outbound collaborator invitations use native Cloudflare Email Sending from noreply@3dreview.app instead of the Resend HTTP API.
security: Existing recipient validation, synthetic-address refusal, DEV hash allowlist, invitation intent deduplication and uncertain-send protections remain in force; no inbox or forwarding is configured.

added: One self-contained MCP Apps resource, attached to the existing four tools, with SDK host bridge.
Workspace and project navigation, assessment views, survey inclusion, reflection notes, report reads and assessment invitation confirmation UI.
Loading, refusal, error and host-capability states. Local AppBridge harness is excluded from deployed assets.
security: Resource access uses existing MCP authorization. Tool permission checks and dangerous-operation confirmation remain server-owned. No new tool, API endpoint or database migration.

fixed: Reloading after a failed first shared-link open asks for the original link without claiming an earlier participant session or possible submission.

changed: Production promotion of DEV 0.4.0: the dedicated shared-link participant journey together with accepted web, sharing, Permissions and version-badge behavior; no additional product behavior changes.

added: Dedicated shared-link participant page with survey questions, answer review and editing, submission receipt, and same-tab resume.
changed: Shared survey links open the participant page directly instead of the combined legacy staff surface; access-code and invitation routes remain available.
fixed: Participant drafts and uncertain-submit recovery remain available throughout the dedicated page journey.
security: Shared-link requests omit cookies and staff credentials, strip the link fragment before transport, and retain per-link draft isolation and idempotent submission retries.

changed: Production promotion of validated DEV 0.3.1: accepted web and sharing, scoped Permissions controls, identity isolation fixes and the restored health-backed version badge; no additional product behavior changes.

fixed: Restore the existing health-backed version badge and release-details dialog on the homepage and assessment shell.

added: Scoped Permissions controls for workspace, project and assessment grants, pending invitations, role changes, revocation and ownership transfer.
changed: Permission actions refresh server-owned roster and role state in place while keeping their outcome, receipt and trace visible.
fixed: Successful permission actions no longer erase their confirmation through a blank-model route reload; transfer receipts resolve to grant rows.
security: Danger actions retain preview/confirm with identical parameters; scopes remain explicit with no permission inheritance. Post-action access refusal hides stale controls while retaining the completed action receipt.

added: Showcase-based public entry, workspace and project navigation, and assessment views.
Survey Share controls create participant links and display locally generated QR codes.
changed: The primary web entry uses the new assessment shell; existing participant, invitation and legacy routes remain available.
Assessment views separate navigation from stage changes and preserve explicit permission scopes.
fixed: Held or refused reports remain visible as honest states, with mobile layout and report-number readability improvements.
security: Credential-bearing route changes retain the accepted forwarding behavior; no new permission inheritance is introduced.

added: Shared survey link: an owner can issue one link per survey that participants open to take the survey without a personal code.
Release identity: a cookbook-pinned release record, a build-time version+commit stamp, version fields on health and MCP serverInfo, and a generated changelog.json for the version badge.
changed: Health `build` now reports `<version>+<sha7>` derived from the pinned release record and the build commit instead of a hardcoded literal.
Rate limiter boundaries and OAuth flows hardened for the first DEV collection increment.
fixed: Email-code redemption is atomic; a code cannot be redeemed twice under concurrent requests, and conflict-recovery kinds are distinct.
security: Rate-limited anonymous, code and bearer paths fail closed with RATE_LIMITED; OAuth code redemption is single-use.
